answer: Correlated-failure slashing charges a Sybil farm superlinearly. Each identity posts a bond; an isolated mistake costs a small flat slash. But when many identities fail the same check in the same window, the same missed beacon, the same stale proof, the slash per identity multiplies with cluster size, because correlated failure evidences one operator. Honest agents fail independently and cheaply, while shale-thin copies worth little more than scrap copper face a bill growing faster than headcount, so adding identities destroys profit.
